base_instruction: You are a helpful event planning assistant. Help the user plan food for a neighborhood block party by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistics. When the user asks you to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

hidden_state.value: You are organizing food for a neighborhood block party. You will introduce attendees and their health details across several turns. Priya's allergy will be UPGRADED from shrimp-only to all shellfish. Mr. Kowalski will drop out. The Chen family will join late. At the end you will share a specific food list and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at which items are problematic — just list them and ask.

You are a calm, friendly neighborhood organizer. You always refer to your neighbors by name in third person (e.g. 'Tom told me...', 'Priya just texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal party planning coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for neighbor updates

ground_truth.answer: Three items have clear problems. Pulled pork sliders on brioche buns: brioche buns are made with wheat flour, which contains gluten — Tom Henderson has celiac disease and cannot eat gluten. Crab cakes: crab is shellfish — Priya's allergy was upgraded from shrimp-only to all shellfish after her allergist confirmed it, so crab cakes are dangerous for her. Brownies with walnuts: standard brownies contain eggs — Lily (David Chen's 7-year-old daughter) broke out in hives from eggs, so brownies are problematic for her. Caesar salad, grilled chicken skewers, and fruit salad are all fine for the current attendees. Mr. Kowalski is no longer attending so his diabetes constraint does not apply — sugary items do not need to be flagged on his account.
required_elements: Pulled pork sliders on brioche buns are problematic for Tom Henderson: brioche buns contain gluten and Tom has celiac disease
Crab cakes are problematic for Priya: her allergy was upgraded to all shellfish (not just shrimp), and crab is shellfish
Brownies with walnuts are problematic for Lily: brownies typically contain eggs and Lily has an egg allergy
Caesar salad is fine for all current attendees
Grilled chicken skewers are fine for all current attendees
Fruit salad is fine for all current attendees
forbidden_elements: Flagging any item for sugar content or diabetes concerns (Mr. Kowalski is no longer attending)
Saying Priya can only not eat shrimp (her constraint was upgraded to all shellfish)
Failing to identify crab cakes as a problem for Priya (crab is shellfish, her upgraded constraint)
Flagging grilled chicken skewers as problematic for any attendee
Flagging Caesar salad as problematic for any attendee
Flagging fruit salad as problematic for any attendee
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint upgrade reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Tom Henderson has celiac disease → no gluten → brioche buns are wheat-based → problematic (inferential chain), (2) Priya's allergy is UPGRADED mid-conversation from shrimp-only to all shellfish after her allergist confirmed it — crab cakes now violate her constraint (constraint upgrade is the primary difficulty mechanism), (3) Lily Chen joins late (turn 3) with an egg allergy inferred from hives after eating scrambled eggs — brownies typically contain eggs (late-joining high-constraint entity), (4) Mr. Kowalski EXITS the party so his diabetes constraint is REMOVED — the agent must NOT flag sugary items on his behalf (removed entity trap), (5) Caesar salad, grilled chicken skewers, and fruit salad are all safe for the current attendee list. The key test is whether the agent applies Priya's UPGRADED shellfish constraint (catching crab cakes) rather than her original shrimp-only constraint, and whether it remembers Lily's egg allergy despite her late introduction and the noise turns creating distance before the probe.

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
